GHK-Cu is one of the most talked-about peptides in anti-aging and biohacking, but what does the science actually say?

This video breaks down how the copper peptide GHK-Cu works, why it naturally declines with age, and how it became linked to skin repair, collagen production, hair growth, and tissue regeneration.
Discovered by biochemist Loren Pickart, GHK-Cu is a tiny three-amino-acid peptide that binds copper and helps deliver it to areas involved in repair. Research has found that it can influence thousands of genes, including pathways associated with inflammation, tissue breakdown, and regeneration. The strongest evidence is in skin and wound healing, where topical GHK-Cu has been studied for its effects on collagen density, firmness, and repair. Early research has also explored possible effects on hair growth and damaged lung tissue, although those areas have much more limited evidence.

Wall Street is freaking out, and the problem isn’t just stocks. The real panic is happening in the U.S. bond market.

As Treasury yields surge to levels not seen in nearly two decades, borrowing costs are rising across the economy. Mortgages remain above 7%, auto loans are becoming harder to afford, credit card balances are compounding faster, and companies refinancing old debt are suddenly facing dramatically higher interest costs.
This video explores why the bond market matters so much to everyday Americans. The Federal Reserve can control short-term interest rates, but longer-term borrowing costs are heavily influenced by investors buying and selling U.S. Treasury debt. And as America’s federal debt pushes past $40 trillion, investors are demanding higher yields to keep financing Washington.
